abstract: In a modern skills-based economy, competency frameworks are essential tools for workforce planning, career progression, and professional development. However, traditional frameworks often exist as static, isolated documents that lack digital connectivity and machine-readability. This article introduces a strategic roadmap to modernise professional standards by applying the FAIR principles: making competency frameworks Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. We present the FAIR competency framework lifecycle, an iterative model centred on end-user engagement, and outline 10 simple rules to guide creators through every stage of development. These rules cover foundational definitions, clear language, persistent identifiers, permissive licensing, and robust governance. By turning frameworks into machine-actionable digital objects, organisations can ensure their standards are easily discoverable, reusable, and ready to integrate into broader learning management systems. Ultimately, adopting these guidelines promotes a more interconnected, transparent, and adaptable global skills landscape where professional expertise can be recognised and shared efficiently.
